contracts.title: MV3-compatible injectable Canvas bitmap processor
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The Junify package accepts an injected ImageBitmap processor, transfers bitmaps through a packaged worker under MV3 strict CSP, and falls back inline without changing the event schema.
contracts.risk_if_broken: The production extension loses Canvas recording, violates MV3 CSP, or emits incompatible events.
contracts.test_notes: Task 5 adds the injectable API, real-browser inline/CSP fallback, worker transfer/error/messageerror/timeout/dispose tests, and unchanged-schema Canvas mutations. The production-packaged browser_extension worker under real MV3 strict CSP remains release-blocking Task 9 evidence, so this cross-repository contract is not promoted.

contracts.title: Canvas capture is non-destructive and closes bitmap resources
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Recording leaves application Canvas 2D/WebGL pixels unchanged, reproduces pixels on replay, closes transferred bitmaps, and stops worker/RAF activity when recording stops.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Recording mutates customer pages or leaks GPU/bitmap resources during long sessions.
contracts.test_notes: Task 5 proves application WebGL screenshots remain unchanged, ImageBitmaps close on all locally owned paths, stop cancels late results and disposes the processor even with recordDOM disabled, and a JSON-persisted candidate artifact replays exact Canvas2D/WebGL pixels in Chrome 151. Production MV3 worker/URL lifetime and repeated long-session cleanup remain Task 9/Task 7 blockers, so this cross-repository contract is not promoted.

contracts.title: Candidate recorder replays in both candidate Junify surfaces
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Artifacts from @junify-app/rrweb@2.1.1-junify.0 replay in the upgraded Rails main player and the explicitly retained static-player surface.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Deploying the recorder after the replayers creates recordings that Junify cannot inspect.
contracts.test_notes: Task 2 adds an official rrweb@2.1.1 real-browser baseline, not the future @junify-app/rrweb@2.1.1-junify.0 candidate. The candidate producer and both cross-repository browser specs remain required.

contracts.title: Historical alpha.4, alpha.19, and alpha.20 artifacts remain replayable
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The candidate replayers consume provenance-locked fixtures produced by rrweb@2.0.0-alpha.4, @junify-app/rrweb@2.0.0-alpha.19, and @junify-app/rrweb@2.0.0-alpha.20.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Existing stored customer sessions become unreadable after the player upgrade.
contracts.test_notes: Task 2 binds alpha.4, Junify alpha.19, and Junify alpha.20 loaded UMD bytes to registry-tarball integrity in yarn.lock, regenerates normalized real-browser artifacts into temporary storage, and replays marker-terminated slices plus full artifacts under official rrweb@2.1.1 in Chrome 151 with no skips. SPA/seek-ready evidence requires target-ID type-3 mutations; stylesheet stages assert computed styles. Task 4 seeks all four accepted artifacts forward and backward with the candidate bundle. Both candidate Rails player surfaces remain required before promotion.

contracts.title: Approximately 13.6 MB CSS FullSnapshot survives transport and replay
contracts.expected_current_behavior: A deterministic roughly 13.6 MB CSS FullSnapshot preserves decoded event count, indexes, bytes, fragment ordering, and gzip digest.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Large real pages produce truncated, reordered, or unreplayable sessions.
contracts.test_notes: Task 2 records a deterministic 13,600,000-byte CSS FullSnapshot with official rrweb@2.1.1 and locks event count, FullSnapshot index/payload digest, raw/gzip digests, and gzip round trip. Extension UTF-8 fragmentation/reassembly remains required before promotion.

contracts.title: Serialized rrweb event format remains unchanged
contracts.expected_current_behavior: For fixed scenarios, decoded events remain wire-compatible; only documented upstream correctness changes may alter payload values.
contracts.risk_if_broken: The service and existing replayers reject or misinterpret newly recorded sessions.
contracts.test_notes: Task 2 authenticates each loaded bundle against its integrity-locked registry tarball, regenerates four comprehensive producers into temporary storage for timestamp-normalized event comparison, and locks browser provenance, event count, FullSnapshot indexes/payload digests, raw/gzip hashes, target-ID mutations, and replayed stage sinks. The future Junify candidate differential and both consumer surfaces remain required before promotion.

contracts.title: Extension events reach real Chrome storage before ingest
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Monotonic indexed events cross the isolated-world bridge, runtime port, and real Chrome storage without loss, duplication, or reordering before V1/V2 flushing.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Unit-green recording silently loses or reorders persisted production events.
contracts.test_notes: Existing integration coverage reaches injection/overlay/mutations but does not observe worker execution, real Chrome storage, or ingest payload.

contracts.title: Recorder stop releases all observers and asynchronous Canvas work
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Stop is idempotent, emits nothing afterward, and repeated start/stop churn does not retain observers, mirrors, RAF callbacks, workers, or detached documents.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Long sessions leak memory/CPU and stopped sessions continue collecting customer activity.
contracts.test_notes: Task 7 plus fix round 1 add real-Chrome source-to-sink gates. Baseline, first, last, and final resource counts are zero across 50 cycles; ten pending-stylesheet cycles retain zero listeners/timers; events remain unchanged after stop and dynamic-password literals remain absent. Focused fixtures prove iframe pagehide/navigation/removal generation disposal, iterative permanent mirror metadata release, shared constructed-stylesheet final-owner release and re-adoption, removed shadow-root silence with replacement liveness, Canvas stop integration, independent cleanup-throw containment, and WebKit untainted-MutationObserver stop/restart. A no-op releaseHost mutation fails the strengthened final-owner gate.

contracts.title: Replayer destroy releases timers, maps, callbacks, and DOM roots
observable_effects: stylesheet load and media metadata listeners
mirror IDs and removed iframe wrapper
no callback, event, or DOM mutation after destroy
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Repeated create/play/seek/destroy cycles clear all owned asynchronous work and references, not only the visible wrapper.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Rails player navigation accumulates retained recordings, iframes, and callbacks.
contracts.test_notes: Task 8 adds a real-Chrome 50-cycle create/play/forward-seek/backward-seek/live/destroy gate. Every cycle starts with four nested iframes, an active Timer action/RAF, fifteen emitter handlers, pending stylesheet and media-metadata listeners, and populated image/canvas/document/legacy/media/mirror sinks. Destroy is idempotent and exception-contained; afterward both state machines are stopped, every count and listener balance is zero, the wrapper is detached, late callbacks/events/DOM mutations remain zero, and final tracked listeners/RAF/timeouts/intervals equal the zero baseline. Review correction ccf6c1f3 adds an authentic throwing-cancelAnimationFrame gate: Timer state/actions invalidate before cancellation and an uncancelled stale RAF runs no callback. Exact malformed legacy media and absent style-rules artifacts survive a temporary JSON persistence round trip while following valid media/style events still reach visible sinks. The Task 4 seek and four-producer historical matrix remain green.

contracts.title: Scoped Junify player bundles the patched local replayer
observable_effects: observed replay module and CSS paths and digests
deterministic production archive and unpacked tree identity
contracts.expected_current_behavior: @junify-app/rrweb-player@2.1.1-junify.0 resolves the patched local Junify replayer and never silently bundles official unpatched @rrweb/replay.
contracts.risk_if_broken: The UI package bypasses the seek fix while appearing to use the Junify player.
contracts.test_notes: Task 3 G-PKG-PLAYER installs exact freshly packed core and player tarballs in an isolated consumer and verifies metadata/files, exact prerelease dependencies, ESM/CJS constructors, real-browser UMD, CSS export/rules, strict declaration resolution, namespace hygiene, and observed local replay module/CSS paths plus SHA-256 digests. A collected mutation proves resolving replay CSS to the official built artifact fails the build. Fix round 3 adds an executable pre/post 18-file content and metadata tree gate around that failing probe, isolates its output from the live player dist, and removes declaration generation from the probe. A Node 20.9 canonical pipeline performs two fresh NODE_ENV=production builds and npm pack --ignore-scripts runs, failing on any archive SHA-256/SHA-512/size or unpacked census/tree drift. Fix round 4 captures a clean HEAD before output, validates the same HEAD plus exact tracked/untracked and generated-residue policy after every clean/build/pack stage and before emission, and uses exactly one npm pack process per run for both absolute package directories with two exact JSON results. The round 3 set is superseded despite matching package bytes because its source state and process contract were not fail-closed. The prior c4bd708d/6b8aaaf9 player remains quarantined; every consumer must revalidate the newest canonical artifact. The boundary deliberately builds upstream packages/rrweb-player/src/main.ts because a wrapper breaks Svelte declaration rollup and would be dead code. No artifact was published.

contracts.title: Only the public Junify rrweb boundary is scoped
observable_effects: deterministic production archive and unpacked tree identity
contracts.expected_current_behavior: @junify-app/rrweb@2.1.1-junify.0 exposes record and Replayer while unmodified internals retain official @rrweb/*, rrweb-snapshot, rrdom, and rrweb package identities.
contracts.risk_if_broken: A global namespace rewrite recreates the 315-file divergence and makes future syncs unsafe.
contracts.test_notes: Task 3 G-PKG-RRWEB installs the exact freshly packed tarball in an isolated consumer and verifies metadata/files, ESM/CJS record and Replayer, real-browser UMD global, CSS, strict ESM/CJS declaration resolution, tarball/dependency/DTS namespace hygiene, and observed local source paths plus SHA-256 digests. Exact declaration diagnostic tuples and fresh declaration digests are pinned; collected same-code occurrence and path-drift probes must fail before the skipLibCheck consumer stage. Fix round 2 adds the browser consumer's exact literal `{ password: true, textarea: true, hidden: true } satisfies NonNullable<Parameters<typeof record>[0]>['maskInputOptions']` compile contract. The public rrweb type intersects the official `rrweb-snapshot@2.1.1` type with `hidden?: boolean`; the official package identity/dependency remains unchanged and no Junify snapshot package exists. Fix round 3 standardizes both boundaries on the same Node 20.9, NODE_ENV=production, npm pack --ignore-scripts pipeline and requires two exact archive and tree identities. Fix round 4 rejects dirty source, generated boundary type/Svelte/tsbuild residue, and HEAD drift before copying any canonical output. Each production run uses one npm pack process with both exact package paths and results. The prior e075ed25 core archive and round 3 manifest are superseded; consumers must revalidate the newest canonical artifact set. No artifact was published.

contracts.title: Sensitive input values never reach persisted event payloads
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Distinct synthetic secrets from password, textarea, placeholder, dynamic type=password, hidden, and sensitive autocomplete cases are absent from initial and mutated persisted payloads.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Credentials or sensitive form values are stored and transmitted despite rendered masking.
contracts.test_notes: Task 6 and fix rounds 1-3 add authentic stable REDs and candidate GREENs for hidden, placeholder, sensitive-autocomplete, and same-batch/synchronous dynamic-password gaps, including post-start assigned and unassigned nodes, temporary password state reached through the type property or setAttribute/removeAttribute, hidden-to-text transitions, and sensitive-autocomplete removal in either mutation order. Snapshot tests, real-Chrome FullSnapshot/Mutation/Input/add tests, and a temporary JSON persisted-artifact scan use unique-length synthetic sentinels with exact node/source/value assertions; missing-event probes reject substitution by a different masked value. Attribute-method hooks restore their exact page-realm prototype identities across idempotent stop/restart and preserve a later third-party patch while making any retained inner rrweb proxy inert before stop returns. Textarea remains protected under the explicit policy, placeholder and autocomplete removal stay null, post-batch normal text stays visible, and no wire schema changes. The contract remains red-known-risk until Task 9 proves absence from real extension Chrome storage and decoded V1/V2 request bodies.

contracts.title: Legacy static player remains a browser compatibility surface
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The alpha.4 static bridge accepts the retained message protocol and replays accepted fixtures with UNSAFE_replayCanvas enabled.
contracts.risk_if_broken: An explicitly retained compatibility surface becomes unusable or diverges silently.
contracts.test_notes: README claims are not coverage; no current browser spec exists and no source reference proves the S3 deployment path is active.

contracts.title: Rails Monitors V1 fetch/decode/replay path renders persisted events
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The /monitors/session_recordings/:id route fetches V1 pages, decodes every stored event, and renders the expected DOM and Canvas with the candidate player.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Legacy stored sessions fail only in the real Monitors route despite unit tests passing.
contracts.test_notes: Current parser/loader and player Jest tests mock network or player; no route-level browser gate exists.

contracts.title: Rails Monitors V2 replay-plan path renders hot and chunk events
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The Monitors route streams ordered chunk and hot segments, parses raw or compatibility-wrapped rrweb events, and renders the persisted session without gaps or duplicate events.
contracts.risk_if_broken: V2 recordings appear truncated, reordered, stuck, or blank in the production route.
contracts.test_notes: Current Jest coverage is local/mocked and does not cross the Rails browser route and persisted read boundary.

contracts.title: Password-rotation artifact decompresses and renders in a real player
contracts.expected_current_behavior: A production-shaped capability-run session_recording artifact is fetched, Base64/gzip-decoded, and visibly replayed with usable controls.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Password-rotation evidence cannot be reviewed even though the artifact exists.
contracts.test_notes: Executable browser coverage exists and the repository records this exact gate; Task 1 did not rerun it. The synthetic fixture has no producer package/version provenance and does not cover the Monitors surfaces.

contracts.title: Explicit forward/backward seek uses the correct real DOM
contracts.expected_current_behavior: An explicit play at a different forward or backward offset does not use a stale virtual DOM for the first synchronization after the seek.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Reviewers see DOM state from the wrong moment immediately after seeking.
contracts.test_notes: Task 4 G-SEEK proves an authentic unmodified-2.1.1 RED and candidate GREEN for forward and backward seeks in real Chrome. The focused legacy-sibling fixture observes public current time plus visible iframe DOM; the authenticated alpha.4, Junify alpha.19, Junify alpha.20, and official 2.1.1 artifacts each pass both candidate seek directions. A 13.6 MB FullSnapshot rebuild also preserves CSSOM rule count and visible DOM while recording an official/candidate timing differential.

contracts.title: Datadog compact serialization is excluded
contracts.expected_current_behavior: This upgrade does not introduce Datadog compact serialization, semantic streams, or a generalized codec framework.
contracts.risk_if_broken: A recorder upgrade becomes an unplanned system-wide storage and replayer migration.
contracts.test_notes: Separate architecture story; no implementation in this patch stack.

contracts.expected_current_behavior: The extension continues to set recordCrossOriginIframes=false; this upgrade does not widen capture scope.
contracts.risk_if_broken: The upgrade expands privacy/security exposure beyond the approved scope.
contracts.test_notes: The focused option test is added with the extension update; feature expansion remains excluded.

contracts.title: Inventory and implementation perform no external release action
contracts.expected_current_behavior: No package publish, release, push, pull request, deploy, or staging action occurs in this work.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Unverified package content reaches consumers or production.
contracts.test_notes: Release operations require separate explicit authorization.

contracts.title: session_recording_service rrweb@^0.9.14 declaration is not a runtime consumer
contracts.expected_current_behavior: The stale rrweb@^0.9.14 declaration has no source import/require/dynamic import and is absent from the built package manifest and deployment zip.
contracts.risk_if_broken: An unrecognized runtime consumer is omitted from the compatibility rollout.
contracts.test_notes: All three censuses currently return no runtime occurrence. Removing the declaration is unrelated cleanup and intentionally excluded.

contracts.title: V1 event transport preserves per-event deflate/base64 JSON
contracts.expected_current_behavior: Each V1 event is JSON-stringified, fflate-compressed, base64-encoded, and sent with its original timestamp/index and first-event metadata.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Legacy ingest or Rails V1 playback receives corrupt or misindexed events.
contracts.test_notes: Unit coverage exists, but the required production-shaped persisted round trip remains open.

contracts.title: V1 and V2 transports preserve the same logical event stream
contracts.expected_current_behavior: After decoding/reassembly, V1 and V2 represent the same fixed-scenario rrweb events apart from V2 transport metadata and its synthetic recording_end event.
contracts.risk_if_broken: Feature-flag selection changes what users can replay instead of only how events are transported.
contracts.test_notes: There is no current real artifact parity gate across both pipelines.

contracts.title: V2 raw-event transport preserves ordering, classification, and fragments
contracts.expected_current_behavior: V2 sorts source events, assigns monotonic 1-based indexes, stores raw JSON eventString, classifies snapshots, fragments oversized UTF-8 bodies without splitting surrogate pairs, and finalizes with recording_end.
contracts.risk_if_broken: V2 replay plans contain gaps, duplicate indexes, bad hashes, or unreconstructable snapshots.
contracts.test_notes: Unit tests do not by themselves close the browser-to-persisted-artifact contract.
